rationale: A defensible extension of the archive's best min-structure, but there is real risk it degenerates into a leverage sort, since the low-leverage z-score will often be the binding leg and low-leverage/high-profitability/high-liquidity is a well-worn safety composite — informative only if diagnosed against the two-leg version rather than reported as an improvement.

Swapping the level for the second moment of gross profitability inside the min is a substantive economic question rather than a cosmetic tweak, though the 5-year VOL requirement will shrink coverage and the earlier volatility-based archive legs were uniformly weak, so expectations should be modest.

This is a plain single-theme liquidity ratio dressed up as an interaction — the numerator double-counts cash (wcap already contains che), the denominator is a scaling variable rather than a distinct "quality theme," and cash/liquidity-to-cost-base runway measures are standard components of published distress scores (Ohlson/Altman-type) with no cross-sectional twist.

The two legs are mechanically anti-correlated because both are functions of pi/at, so within loss-makers the product mostly orders firms by depreciation intensity rather than by "non-cash loss" status, and the archive version already delivered a reliably wrong-signed alpha (t=-2.2) that the "degenerate middle" diagnosis does not convincingly overturn.

A genuinely different channel from the archive (signed cost-ratio dynamics conditioned on liquidity stress) with a coherent sign — the always-positive rank leg leaves the direction to the margin-change z-score exactly as hypothesized — though cogs/revt changes will be noisy for low-revenue firms and should be winsorized or screened.

As a falsification test it is poorly identified: both legs are individually positive return predictors, so MAX will very likely also produce a positive alpha (it is nearly the average of the two legs plus a convexity term), meaning the result cannot distinguish complementarity from the component premia and the proposal reduces to an operator-flipped duplicate of the archive winner.
